questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after a car struck her from the side at an intersection. She reports that she never saw the other car approaching. She has had daily headaches for the past 2 months. On examination she has markedly decreased bilateral peripheral vision. Compression of which of the following structures best explains her visual findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cavernous sinus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Left optic nerve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Occipital visual cortex

choices.label: D
choices.text: Optic chiasm

choices.label: E
choices.text: Right optic tract

explanation.summary: A sellar mass growing upward compresses the crossing fibers at the optic chiasm and produces bitemporal hemianopia.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pituitary sits in the sella turcica immediately inferior to the optic chiasm. As an adenoma enlarges it presses on the decussating fibers, knocking out both temporal visual fields and leaving the patient without peripheral vision on either side. That is why she failed to see a car approaching from the side, and impaired vision is the most common presenting complaint of a pituitary adenoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cavernous sinus involvement causes cranial nerve palsies with impaired eye movements rather than field loss.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Compression of a single optic nerve causes monocular vision loss, not a symmetric bilateral peripheral deficit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Occipital cortex injury also gives a homonymous field cut and is not caused by a sellar mass.
whyWrongByChoice.E: An optic tract lesion produces a homonymous hemianopia, losing the same side of the field in both eyes.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man is evaluated for 3 months of headaches and blurred vision. Neurologic examination is otherwise normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next diagnostic step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Carotid duplex ultrasonography

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lumbar puncture with opening pressure

choices.label: C
choices.text: MRI of the pituitary

choices.label: D
choices.text: Skull radiography of the sella turcica

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transsphenoidal biopsy of the gland

explanation.summary: Acute headaches with visual field deficits warrant MRI of the pituitary to confirm or exclude an adenoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture directs that any patient with acute headaches and/or visual field deficits should have an MRI of the pituitary to confirm the presence of an adenoma. Once a mass is found, paired testing of pituitary hormones and their target-gland hormones follows to determine whether it is functioning.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Imaging the carotid arteries addresses vascular disease, not a compressive sellar lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Measuring cerebrospinal fluid pressure does not localize or characterize a sellar tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plain radiography cannot resolve a small sellar mass or its relationship to the optic chiasm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tissue sampling comes after imaging identifies a lesion; it is not the first diagnostic step.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman reports 8 months of amenorrhea, difficulty conceiving, and milky nipple discharge. MRI shows a 6-mm sellar mass. Serum prolactin is markedly elevated. Which of the following best explains her amenorrhea?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prolactin accelerates hepatic clearance of circulating estrogen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prolactin binds and activates the LH receptor in the ovary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prolactin directly destroys ovarian granulosa cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolactin suppresses hypothalamic GnRH, lowering LH and FSH

choices.label: E
choices.text: The mass compresses gonadotrophs, blocking GnRH synthesis

explanation.summary: Hyperprolactinemia causes hypogonadism by suppressing hypothalamic GnRH and therefore pituitary LH and FSH.
explanation.whyCorrect: High prolactin levels suppress hypothalamic production of gonadotropin-releasing hormone. Less GnRH reaching the anterior pituitary means less LH and FSH secretion, which disrupts the menstrual cycle and produces irregular or absent menses and infertility. Galactorrhea and reduced libido round out the prolactinoma picture.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estrogen falls because the ovary is understimulated, not because prolactin speeds its clearance.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Prolactin acts through its own receptor and does not stimulate ovarian LH receptors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prolactin does not lyse ovarian cells; the defect is a functional loss of gonadotropin drive.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GnRH is made in the hypothalamus, not by pituitary gonadotrophs, and a 6-mm lesion exerts no mass effect.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman presents with galactorrhea and is found to have a pituitary mass with an elevated serum prolactin level. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cabergoline

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lanreotide

choices.label: C
choices.text: Octreotide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pituitary radiation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transsphenoidal surgery

explanation.summary: Prolactinomas are the one pituitary adenoma treated medically first, with a dopamine agonist.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cabergoline is a long-acting dopamine-receptor agonist that reproduces the physiologic inhibitory signal on lactotrophs. It lowers serum prolactin, restores gonadal function, and shrinks the tumor, and it is preferred over bromocriptine because it is more effective and better tolerated.

whyWrongByChoice.B: This somatostatin analog likewise targets GH-secreting tumors, not lactotroph adenomas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This somatostatin analog is used for GH excess in patients who cannot undergo surgery.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Irradiation is used only when patients do not respond to or cannot receive medical and surgical therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surgery is reserved for prolactinomas that fail or cannot tolerate dopamine agonist therapy.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man reports that his wedding ring and shoes no longer fit and that his wife has noticed loud snoring with witnessed apneas. Examination shows coarse facial features, thickened skin, and a protruding jaw. MRI shows a 14-mm sellar mass. Excess of which of the following hormones best explains his findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenocorticotropic hormone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Growth hormone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolactin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thyroid-stimulating hormone

explanation.summary: GH excess after epiphyseal closure produces acromegaly, including obstructive sleep apnea.
explanation.whyCorrect: A somatotroph adenoma floods an adult whose epiphyseal plates are already fused, so growth is appositional rather than linear: coarsened facial features, enlarged hands, thickened skin, and prognathism. Pharyngeal soft tissue growth causes obstructive sleep apnea, and other complications include hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, hypertension, arthritis, and increased risk of thyroid and colorectal cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ACTH excess produces moon facies, purple striae, and truncal obesity rather than prognathism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gonadotropin excess is typically clinically silent and does not alter facial bones or skin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolactin excess causes galactorrhea, low libido, and menstrual disturbance, not acral enlargement.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TSH excess drives hyperthyroidism with weight loss, anxiety, and palpitations.

questions.stem: A 13-year-old boy is in the 99th percentile for height and has grown 6 inches in the past year. MRI shows a pituitary macroadenoma, and growth hormone levels are markedly elevated. Which of the following best explains why he develops gigantism rather than acromegaly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adolescent cartilage cannot respond to growth hormone at all

choices.label: B
choices.text: Children lack the somatostatin feedback that limits growth hormone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Growth hormone receptors are absent from adult periosteum

choices.label: D
choices.text: His epiphyseal growth plates have not yet fused

choices.label: E
choices.text: His tumor secretes more growth hormone than an adult tumor

explanation.summary: Whether GH excess causes gigantism or acromegaly depends entirely on epiphyseal plate status.
explanation.whyCorrect: In children the epiphyseal plates are still open, so excess GH drives unchecked linear growth and the child becomes abnormally tall. Once the plates close in adulthood, the same hormonal excess can no longer lengthen bone and instead produces the acral and facial coarsening of acromegaly.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Growth plate cartilage is highly responsive to GH, which is the reason linear growth accelerates.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Children retain normal hypothalamic-pituitary regulation; the tumor secretes autonomously at any age.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adults still respond to GH, which is precisely why they develop acromegalic soft tissue and bone changes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The syndrome is determined by skeletal maturity, not by how much hormone the tumor makes.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old woman has a 1-year history of weight gain, hypertension, and purple abdominal striae. She has also noticed progressive darkening of her skin, including her palmar creases. MRI shows an 8-mm pituitary lesion. Which of the following best explains her skin darkening?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenal androgen excess drives melanocyte proliferation in the skin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cortisol directly stimulates melanocytes to increase melanin synthesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cortisol thins the epidermis so dermal pigment becomes visible

choices.label: D
choices.text: Growth hormone co-secretion thickens and darkens the skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Melanocyte-stimulating hormone from the ACTH precursor activates MCR1

explanation.summary: Hyperpigmentation distinguishes secondary (ACTH-driven) hypercortisolism from primary hypercortisolism.
explanation.whyCorrect: A corticotroph adenoma drives the adrenal gland to overproduce cortisol, which is Cushing disease. Melanocyte-stimulating hormone comes from the same precursor hormone as ACTH, and both can activate MCR1 to increase melanin production, so patients with pituitary-driven disease darken. That feature is seen in secondary but not primary hypercortisolism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Androgens cause hirsutism and acne rather than the diffuse darkening described here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cortisol produces striae, central obesity, and hyperglycemia, but it does not pigment the skin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Skin thinning is a cortisol effect, yet patients with primary hypercortisolism thin without darkening.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This lesion is driving cortisol excess, and GH thickens skin without causing hyperpigmentation.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman has 4 months of weight loss, anxiety, diarrhea, moist skin, and palpitations. Free T4 and total T3 are elevated, and serum TSH is also elevated. Which of the following adenoma types is most likely responsible?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Corticotroph adenoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gonadotroph adenoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lactotroph adenoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Somatotroph adenoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thyrotroph adenoma

explanation.summary: Hyperthyroid symptoms with a high TSH and high thyroid hormones point to a TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: A thyrotroph adenoma secretes TSH autonomously, so it keeps triggering the thyroid gland to release excess T4 and T3 despite the negative feedback that should shut TSH off. The resulting secondary hyperthyroidism gives weight loss, anxiety, diarrhea, moist skin, and heart palpitations. Paired testing of TSH with T4 is what exposes the pattern.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ACTH excess yields cortisol-driven features such as striae and truncal obesity, not thyrotoxicosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gonadotropin-secreting tumors are generally clinically silent and leave thyroid tests normal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prolactin excess causes galactorrhea and menstrual irregularity, and it does not raise thyroid hormones.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GH excess produces acromegaly; thyroid function tests are not driven up by a somatotroph tumor.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with acromegaly and a 15-mm pituitary adenoma has severe cardiopulmonary disease that makes him a poor operative candidate. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bromocriptine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cabergoline

choices.label: C
choices.text: Observation with serial imaging

choices.label: D
choices.text: Octreotide

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transsphenoidal surgery

explanation.summary: Somatostatin analogs are the fallback for GH-secreting adenomas when surgery is not possible.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most GH-secreting adenomas are treated with transsphenoidal resection, but when a patient cannot undergo surgery, high GH is treated with octreotide or lanreotide. These somatostatin analogs both lower GH levels and reduce the size of the adenoma. The same agents are used to suppress TSH production before resection of a thyrotroph adenoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This dopamine agonist is an alternative for prolactinoma and does not control GH excess.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dopamine agonists are directed at prolactinomas, not at somatotroph adenomas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Untreated GH excess carries cardiomyopathy, apnea, and cancer risk, so watchful waiting is inappropriate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surgery is the usual first choice for GH-secreting tumors but is excluded by his operative risk.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman with a known pituitary macroadenoma develops sudden severe headache, vomiting, and diplopia, then becomes unresponsive. Imaging shows abrupt enlargement of the sellar mass with internal hemorrhage. Which of the following best describes this event?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cavernous sinus thrombosis complicating a sellar tumor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Malignant transformation of a pituitary adenoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obstructive hydrocephalus from suprasellar extension

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pituitary apoplexy, a neurosurgical emergency

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sheehan syndrome from peripartum pituitary infarction

explanation.summary: Acute hemorrhage into a pituitary tumor with rapid expansion and loss of consciousness is pituitary apoplexy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bleeding into a pituitary neoplasm can enlarge the lesion abruptly and cause loss of consciousness. This situation is termed pituitary apoplexy, and because it may be rapidly fatal it is treated as a neurosurgical emergency rather than managed medically.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sinus thrombosis presents with orbital congestion and ophthalmoplegia, not intratumoral bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malignant pituitary tumors are very rare and would not produce a sudden hemorrhagic collapse.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hydrocephalus follows gradual extension beyond the sella and would not show internal hemorrhage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: That syndrome is postpartum infarction of the gland causing hormone deficiency, not tumor hemorrhage.

questions.stem: A 51-year-old man undergoes resection of a sellar mass. Histologic sections show sheets and cords of uniform polygonal cells, and a reticulin stain shows loss of the normal supporting network. Which of the following conclusions is best supported by these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The lesion arises from the posterior pituitary lobe

choices.label: B
choices.text: The tissue is a pituitary adenoma rather than normal anterior pituitary

choices.label: C
choices.text: The tissue is normal anterior pituitary displaced by an adjacent mass

choices.label: D
choices.text: The tumor is a nonfunctioning gonadotroph subtype specifically

choices.label: E
choices.text: The tumor is a pituitary carcinoma with early metastatic potential

explanation.summary: Cellular monomorphism plus an absent reticulin network are the two morphologic hallmarks of a pituitary adenoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Typical adenomas are composed of monomorphic polygonal cells in sheets or cords with sparse reticulin, which is why they feel soft and gelatinous. Those two features are exactly what distinguish adenoma from normal anterior pituitary parenchyma, where varied cell types sit within an intact reticulin framework.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The posterior lobe is neural tissue; adenomas causing hyperpituitarism arise in the anterior lobe.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Normal parenchyma is cytologically heterogeneous and retains its reticulin network.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Assigning a cell lineage requires immunostains for hormones and transcription factors, not these findings.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Malignant pituitary tumors are very rare, and monomorphism with reticulin loss does not indicate carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman is evaluated for headaches and polyuria. Laboratory studies show elevated levels of both an anterior pituitary hormone and antidiuretic hormone. Which of the following is the most likely site of the underlying pathology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenal cortex

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anterior pituitary lobe

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypothalamus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Posterior pituitary lobe

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thyroid gland

explanation.summary: When posterior as well as anterior pituitary hormones are elevated, the lesion lies in the hypothalamus.
explanation.whyCorrect: In hyperpituitarism caused by a pituitary adenoma, only anterior pituitary hormones are affected. If posterior pituitary hormones such as antidiuretic hormone are also increased, which is much less common, the pathology instead lies in the hypothalamus, because that is where the posterior hormones are produced. Hypothalamic disorders are one of the listed causes of hyperpituitarism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adrenal pathology raises cortisol while suppressing ACTH and has no effect on antidiuretic hormone.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An anterior lobe adenoma raises anterior hormones alone and cannot drive antidiuretic hormone up.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The posterior lobe only stores and releases hormones that the hypothalamus synthesizes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thyroid disease alters T4 and T3 and would not elevate an anterior hormone plus antidiuretic hormone.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman is evaluated 6 weeks after delivering twins. Her delivery was complicated by a large postpartum hemorrhage. She reports exhaustion, dry skin, and hair loss, and says she had to stop breastfeeding because no milk was produced. Her blood pressure is 94/56 mm Hg and her pulse is irregular. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Empty sella syndrome

choices.label: B
choices.text: Granulomatous infiltration of the sella turcica

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pituitary apoplexy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rathke cleft cyst

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sheehan syndrome

explanation.summary: Postpartum hemorrhage followed by hypotension, lethargy, and failure to lactate is the classic presentation of Sheehan syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sheehan syndrome is infarction of the pituitary gland after postpartum hemorrhage; the gland is enlarged in pregnancy and is vulnerable to ischemia during hypovolemic shock. Loss of one or more pituitary hormones follows, with the initial symptoms of hypotension, then lethargy, anorexia, weight loss, and inability to breastfeed. Her failure to lactate reflects prolactin deficiency, and her fatigue and dry skin reflect loss of TSH drive to the thyroid.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Empty sella syndrome is an incidental imaging finding in which CSF flattens the gland, and pituitary hormone levels are usually normal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Granulomatous disease such as sarcoidosis can compress the gland, but nothing here suggests a systemic inflammatory disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Apoplexy is sudden hemorrhage into the gland, presenting with abrupt excruciating headache and diplopia rather than a slow postpartum decline.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A Rathke cleft cyst expands slowly with proteinaceous fluid and has no relationship to obstetric hemorrhage.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman with newly diagnosed panhypopituitarism after pituitary surgery has a low serum cortisol and a low free thyroxine. She is scheduled to begin hormone replacement. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step in her therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin desmopressin before starting any other replacement

choices.label: B
choices.text: Begin estrogen replacement before starting levothyroxine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Begin glucocorticoid replacement before starting levothyroxine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Begin levothyroxine and recombinant growth hormone together

choices.label: E
choices.text: Begin levothyroxine before starting glucocorticoid replacement

explanation.summary: When ACTH deficiency is known or suspected, glucocorticoids must be replaced before thyroid hormone.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thyroid hormone raises metabolic demand and accelerates cortisol clearance, so starting levothyroxine in a patient with untreated cortisol deficiency can precipitate an adrenal crisis. The lecture states this as an essential treatment principle in hypopituitarism. Once glucocorticoid replacement is established, levothyroxine can be started safely.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Desmopressin treats vasopressin deficiency, which does not usually accompany anterior pituitary deficiency and is not the urgent issue here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gonadotropin deficiency causes infertility and hypogonadal symptoms but carries no acute risk that outranks cortisol replacement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Growth hormone deficiency is not acutely life-threatening, and levothyroxine still must not precede glucocorticoids.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This is the exact sequence that precipitates adrenal crisis in a patient with untreated ACTH deficiency.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man with a known pituitary macroadenoma comes to the emergency department with the sudden onset of an excruciating headache and double vision. His blood pressure is 84/50 mm Hg and he is drowsy. Which of the following best describes the underlying pathologic event?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Expansion of a cyst lined by ciliated cuboidal epithelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Granulomatous inflammation infiltrating the sella turcica

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hemorrhage into the gland with rapid expansion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Herniation of cerebrospinal fluid into the sella turcica

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ischemic infarction of the gland after obstetric hemorrhage

explanation.summary: Pituitary apoplexy is sudden hemorrhage into the pituitary gland, often occurring within an existing adenoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Apoplexy classically produces an abrupt, excruciating headache with diplopia from pressure on the oculomotor nerves, together with acute hypopituitarism. Loss of ACTH and therefore cortisol explains his hypotension, and severe cases progress to cardiovascular collapse, loss of consciousness, and death. It requires urgent assessment of visual acuity and fields, cranial nerve function, and level of consciousness, plus endocrinology and neurosurgical consultation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: That epithelial lining describes a Rathke cleft cyst, which enlarges gradually rather than causing a thunderclap presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Granulomatous involvement of the sella by sarcoidosis or granulomatosis with polyangiitis compresses the gland over time, not in minutes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CSF filling the sella describes empty sella syndrome, an incidental finding that usually causes no symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Infarction of the gland after postpartum hemorrhage describes Sheehan syndrome, which cannot apply to this patient.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man develops panhypopituitarism after sustaining head trauma in a motor vehicle collision. He is hypotensive and lethargic. Replacement of which of the following hormones is most important in his acute management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cortisol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Growth hormone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prolactin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Testosterone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thyroxine

explanation.summary: Cortisol replacement is the priority in panhypopituitarism because cortisol maintains peripheral vascular tone and blood pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: ACTH deficiency produces cortisol deficiency, whose most dangerous consequences are hypoglycemia, hypotension, and death from vascular collapse. Stabilizing the circulation is the critical first task in managing hypopituitarism, so glucocorticoid is given parenterally without waiting for confirmatory testing. The other deficiencies matter for long-term health but are not acutely lethal.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Growth hormone deficiency causes altered body composition and low bone density, neither of which is an acute threat.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prolactin deficiency impairs lactation only, and no routine prolactin replacement product exists.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Testosterone deficiency causes low libido, infertility, and low energy, none of which are life-threatening.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thyroid hormone is needed eventually but must follow glucocorticoids, since giving it first can precipitate adrenal crisis.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman undergoes brain MRI for evaluation of chronic migraines. The sella turcica is enlarged and filled with cerebrospinal fluid, with the pituitary seen as a thin crescent at its base. Serum cortisol, free thyroxine, TSH, and IGF-1 are all normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Empty sella syndrome

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pituitary macroadenoma expanding the sella

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rathke cleft cyst

choices.label: D
choices.text: Septo-optic dysplasia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sheehan syndrome

explanation.summary: An enlarged, CSF-filled sella with a flattened gland and normal hormone levels is empty sella syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: In empty sella syndrome, a weakness in the sellar diaphragm or a high CSF volume allows the subarachnoid space to herniate into the sella, flattening the gland so that it appears absent. It is typically discovered incidentally on MRI or CT obtained for another reason and usually causes no harm. Patients characteristically have normal pituitary hormone levels.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A macroadenoma appears as a mass expanding out of the sella, not as CSF replacing the sellar contents.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A Rathke cleft cyst is a discrete cystic lesion containing proteinaceous fluid that compresses the gland.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Septo-optic dysplasia is a congenital HESX1-associated brain malformation presenting in childhood, not an incidental adult finding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sheehan syndrome follows postpartum hemorrhage and produces measurable hormone deficiencies, not a normal panel.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man is recovering from a severe traumatic brain injury. Over 2 days he produces 7 L of dilute urine, becomes intensely thirsty, and is found to have a serum sodium of 152 mEq/L. Which of the following test results would best confirm the suspected diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Urine osmolality falls further after administration of synthetic ADH

choices.label: B
choices.text: Urine osmolality remains unchanged after both water deprivation and synthetic ADH

choices.label: C
choices.text: Urine osmolality rises after synthetic ADH but not with water deprivation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Urine osmolality rises appropriately with water deprivation alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urine osmolality rises with water deprivation but not after synthetic ADH

explanation.summary: Arginine vasopressin deficiency is confirmed when dilute polyuria concentrates in response to exogenous ADH but not to water deprivation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vasopressin deficiency, formerly called central diabetes insipidus, occurs most often after head trauma or intracranial surgery, and it causes the kidney to excrete large volumes of dilute urine with dehydration, hypernatremia, thirst, and dizziness. The workup shows increased urine volume with decreased urine osmolarity that resolves after giving synthetic ADH but not with water deprivation. That pattern proves the kidney can respond and that the missing element is the hormone itself.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Giving ADH to a patient lacking it concentrates the urine; a further fall in osmolality is not a recognized response.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No response to either maneuver would not localize the defect to a missing pituitary hormone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An appropriate response to water deprivation alone indicates that endogenous ADH is being released normally.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Concentrating with deprivation but failing to respond to hormone is the opposite of a hormone-deficient kidney.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy is evaluated for short stature that has worsened relative to his peers over 3 years. He has no chronic illness and his nutrition is adequate. Which of the following laboratory studies is most useful in evaluating him for growth hormone deficiency?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Random serum growth hormone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Serum antidiuretic hormone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serum calcitonin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum IGF-1 (somatomedin C)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum prolactin

explanation.summary: Growth hormone deficiency is assessed with bone age and IGF-1, not with a direct growth hormone level.
explanation.whyCorrect: Growth hormone is secreted in pulses, so a single random level fluctuates too much to be interpretable; IGF-1 integrates growth hormone action over time and is the standard surrogate. The primary workup for suspected GH deficiency is bone age plus a low IGF-1. In children, GH deficiency typically presents exactly as this boy does, with short stature.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Growth hormone levels fluctuate so widely that a random measurement is not used to establish deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ADH levels are not routinely measured, and its deficiency causes dilute polyuria rather than growth failure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Calcitonin lowers serum calcium and is not a pituitary hormone, so it plays no role here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prolactin deficiency causes failure of lactation and would not explain or evaluate short stature.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old woman treated with cranial radiation 8 years ago now has fatigue, weight loss, and postural dizziness, and panhypopituitarism is suspected. Measurement of which of the following serum hormone levels would be most helpful in her evaluation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antidiuretic hormone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Calcitonin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Corticotropin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Growth hormone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Insulin

explanation.summary: ACTH, measured with cortisol, is the most useful hormone to check when panhypopituitarism is suspected.
explanation.whyCorrect: ACTH falls in panhypopituitarism, and the resulting cortisol deficiency is the deficit that threatens life through hypotension and hypoglycemia. Pituitary hormones should be tested in pairs with their target gland hormone, so low ACTH with low cortisol establishes central adrenal insufficiency and can be confirmed with an ACTH stimulation test. Radiation therapy given to eliminate residual tumor cells is a recognized cause of delayed pituitary failure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ADH can fall in pituitary disease, but its level is not routinely measured; the diagnosis rests on urine volume and osmolarity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Calcitonin lowers serum calcium and is not produced by the pituitary at all.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Growth hormone falls in some patients but fluctuates too much to measure directly; IGF-1 is used instead.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Insulin comes from pancreatic beta cells and drives glycogen synthesis; it is not part of a pituitary workup.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman with hypopituitarism has been receiving hydrocortisone for 2 weeks, and levothyroxine has now been started for TSH deficiency. Which of the following is the most appropriate laboratory parameter for adjusting her levothyroxine dose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Free thyroxine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Insulin-like growth factor 1

choices.label: C
choices.text: Morning serum cortisol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum thyroglobulin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum TSH

explanation.summary: In central (TSH-deficient) hypothyroidism, levothyroxine therapy is monitored with free T4 rather than TSH.
explanation.whyCorrect: The failing pituitary cannot mount a normal TSH response, so TSH no longer reflects whether the replacement dose is adequate. Free T4 measures the delivered hormone directly and is the parameter used to titrate therapy in this setting. Follow-up should also watch for signs of both under-replacement and over-replacement.

whyWrongByChoice.B: IGF-1 monitors growth hormone replacement, not levothyroxine dosing.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Morning cortisol relates to glucocorticoid replacement and says nothing about thyroid dosing.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thyroglobulin is not used to titrate thyroid hormone replacement in hypopituitarism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TSH is unreliable here precisely because the pituitary that would generate it is the diseased organ.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with known hypopituitarism is brought to the emergency department with vomiting, confusion, a blood pressure of 78/44 mm Hg, and a blood glucose of 46 mg/dL. Adrenal crisis is suspected. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin a water deprivation test to clarify the hormone deficiency

choices.label: B
choices.text: Give intravenous hydrocortisone now, drawing cortisol only if it causes no delay

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give intravenous levothyroxine before any glucocorticoid is administered

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obtain a pituitary MRI before any hormone therapy is started

choices.label: E
choices.text: Withhold treatment until the serum cortisol and ACTH results return

explanation.summary: Suspected adrenal crisis is treated immediately with parenteral hydrocortisone; confirmatory testing must never delay therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blood may be collected for cortisol and ACTH before treatment, but testing must not postpone glucocorticoid administration when adrenal crisis is suspected. A commonly recommended adult regimen begins with 100 mg of hydrocortisone intravenously or intramuscularly, followed by stress doses until clinical recovery. Isotonic saline and dextrose are given alongside it because he is hypotensive and hypoglycemic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Water deprivation testing evaluates polyuria and would be dangerous in a hypotensive, dehydrated patient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Thyroid hormone given before glucocorticoids can precipitate or worsen adrenal crisis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Imaging is part of the workup but never precedes resuscitation of an unstable patient.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Waiting for results in a hypotensive, hypoglycemic patient risks vascular collapse and death.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman has had no menstrual periods for 8 months following resection of a sellar mass. She reports hot flashes, vaginal dryness, and decreased libido. Which of the following laboratory patterns is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: High FSH, high LH, and high estradiol

choices.label: B
choices.text: High FSH, high LH, and low estradiol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Low FSH, low LH, and high estradiol

choices.label: D
choices.text: Low FSH, low LH, and low estradiol

choices.label: E
choices.text: Normal FSH, normal LH, and high prolactin

explanation.summary: Pituitary gonadotropin deficiency produces hypogonadotropic hypogonadism: low FSH and LH with low sex steroid levels.
explanation.whyCorrect: Damage to the gonadotrophs during resection of a sellar mass removes FSH and LH drive, so the ovary is never stimulated and estradiol falls. Low estradiol explains her amenorrhea, hot flashes, and vaginal atrophy and dryness, and it also causes infertility. The workup for this axis is low FSH, LH, and estradiol in women, or low morning testosterone in men.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Uniformly high gonadotropins and estradiol do not fit a destroyed pituitary or explain her hypoestrogenic symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: High gonadotropins with low estradiol indicate primary ovarian failure, in which the pituitary is intact and responding.
whyWrongByChoice.C: High estradiol would suppress rather than produce hot flashes and vaginal dryness.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hypopituitarism after resection causes prolactin deficiency, and hyperprolactinemia would not explain her hypoestrogenic symptoms.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man has low cortisol, low free thyroxine, and low morning testosterone, each with an inappropriately low corresponding pituitary hormone. He also passes 6 L of dilute urine daily and has a serum sodium of 149 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely site of his underlying lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenal cortex

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anterior pituitary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypothalamus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Posterior pituitary

choices.label: E
choices.text: Renal collecting duct

explanation.summary: Anterior pituitary failure accompanied by diabetes insipidus points to a hypothalamic rather than a pituitary lesion.
explanation.whyCorrect: When hypopituitarism is accompanied by evidence of posterior pituitary dysfunction in the form of diabetes insipidus, the disorder is almost always of hypothalamic origin. His dilute polyuria with hypernatremia signals vasopressin deficiency, and his low cortisol, thyroxine, and testosterone with low trophic hormones signal anterior lobe failure. A single lesion explaining both must sit above the gland, in the hypothalamus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adrenal cortical disease would raise ACTH and could not account for the low thyroxine and testosterone.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An isolated anterior pituitary lesion produces the anterior deficits but does not typically cause diabetes insipidus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A posterior lobe lesion would explain the dilute polyuria alone and not the multiple anterior hormone deficiencies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Collecting duct resistance to ADH is nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, which does not cause pituitary hormone deficiencies.

questions.stem: A 49-year-old woman is evaluated for frustrating joint aches, frequent headaches, and worsening peripheral vision. She uses CPAP for obstructive sleep apnea. She reports that over the past few years she has had to buy larger shoes and have her rings resized. Which of the following is the best initial test to evaluate her suspected condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arginine-stimulated growth hormone concentration

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contrast-enhanced MRI of the sella turcica

choices.label: C
choices.text: Random serum growth hormone concentration

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum insulin-like growth factor binding protein 3

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum insulin-like growth factor-1 concentration

explanation.summary: Serum IGF-1 is the best initial test when acromegaly is suspected.
explanation.whyCorrect: Her enlarging hands and feet, coarsening features, snoring, joint pain, headaches, and visual field loss point to a GH-secreting pituitary adenoma. Because random GH levels fluctuate widely through the day, IGF-1 is used as the screening measure; if it is elevated, a GH suppression test follows and imaging is obtained after the diagnosis is made.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Provocative stimulation with arginine is used to diagnose GH deficiency, not GH excess.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pituitary MRI is performed after biochemical diagnosis, to localize the adenoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GH secretion is pulsatile, so a single random level is unreliable for detecting GH excess.
whyWrongByChoice.D: IGFBP-3 is a supplementary measure in uncertain cases of GH deficiency, not a screen for excess.

questions.stem: An 8-year-old boy has fallen from the 25th to the 3rd percentile for height over 3 years. His pediatrician orders a serum IGF-1 level rather than a random serum growth hormone level. Which of the following best explains this choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IGF-1 is produced by the pituitary and GH is produced by the liver

choices.label: B
choices.text: IGF-1 is stable while GH is secreted in pulses through the day

choices.label: C
choices.text: IGF-1 is unaffected by thyroid disease while GH is not

choices.label: D
choices.text: IGF-1 mediates bone growth while GH acts only on muscle

choices.label: E
choices.text: IGF-1 rises only after the epiphyseal plates have fused

explanation.summary: IGF-1 is the better screening test because it reflects integrated GH secretion without pulsatile swings.
explanation.whyCorrect: GH is released in pulses and varies widely over the course of a day, so a single value is hard to interpret. IGF-1 is generated by the liver in response to GH and stays relatively constant, making it a stable indicator of GH secretion; in GH deficiency it is low and bone age is delayed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The relationship is reversed: GH comes from the anterior pituitary and stimulates hepatic IGF-1 production.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypothyroidism is one of the conditions that must be excluded when evaluating growth failure, and it is not the reason IGF-1 is preferred.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GH and IGF-1 act together on both bone and muscle rather than dividing those tissues between them.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IGF-1 mediates growth at open epiphyseal plates and is measurable throughout childhood.

questions.stem: A 3-year-old boy has severe growth failure, small head circumference, a prominent forehead, a saddle nose, and small genitalia. He has had episodes of fasting hypoglycemia. Laboratory studies show a markedly elevated serum growth hormone level with a low IGF-1 level. Genetic testing reveals a growth hormone receptor mutation. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Levothyroxine replacement therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Octreotide, a somatostatin analog

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recombinant growth hormone injections

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recombinant IGF-1 injections

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surgical resection of a pituitary adenoma

explanation.summary: Laron syndrome is GH insensitivity from a GH receptor mutation and is managed with recombinant IGF-1.
explanation.whyCorrect: This autosomal recessive receptor defect leaves the liver unable to sense GH, so IGF-1 is low while GH rises from loss of feedback inhibition. Because the receptor cannot respond, giving more GH is futile; there is no cure, and treatment is medical management with recombinant IGF-1 injections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hypothyroidism is a separate cause of growth failure and is not the defect identified here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Octreotide suppresses GH secretion and is used for GH excess, which would worsen this child's low IGF-1.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GH cannot work through a mutated, insensitive receptor, so replacement would not raise IGF-1 or restore growth.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The problem is a peripheral receptor mutation, not a hormone-secreting pituitary tumor.

questions.stem: A 20-month-old girl with complete congenital growth hormone deficiency confirmed by genetic testing has grown normally along the 50th percentile for length since birth. Which of the following best explains her normal growth so far?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cortisol substitutes for growth hormone at the growth plate in infancy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epiphyseal plates are not responsive to any hormone before age 2

choices.label: C
choices.text: Insulin is the dominant driver of skeletal growth until puberty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maternal growth hormone crosses the placenta and persists in infancy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thyroid hormone is the primary growth stimulus in the first 2 years

explanation.summary: Growth in the first 2 years is driven mainly by thyroid hormone, so congenital GH deficiency is rarely detected in infancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Children with complete congenital GH deficiency grow normally for roughly the first 2 years and then show a decline in growth velocity, which is why the diagnosis is rare in newborns. Infants are usually identified only when another sign such as neonatal hypoglycemia or ambiguous genitalia prompts evaluation, and this is a reason annual primary care visits matter beyond the immunization period.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cortisol is not the growth stimulus of infancy and does not substitute for GH at the plate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The growth plates are hormonally responsive in infancy; thyroid hormone is what is driving them.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin is antagonized by GH in glucose handling and is not described as the driver of linear growth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Normal early growth is attributed to the infant's own thyroid hormone, not to transplacental GH.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old girl is brought in because she has become the shortest child in her class. Her height has dropped below her established growth centile over the past 2 years, and her weight-to-height ratio is increased. Physical examination is otherwise unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in evaluation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin a trial of recombinant growth hormone injections

choices.label: B
choices.text: Evaluate for hypothyroidism and Turner syndrome

choices.label: C
choices.text: Measure IGF-binding protein 3 to confirm the diagnosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obtain MRI of the sella turcica to look for a mass

choices.label: E
choices.text: Perform a growth hormone stimulation test with clonidine

explanation.summary: Commoner causes of growth failure must be excluded before pursuing a GH axis workup.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chronic infections, hypothyroidism, Turner syndrome, and bone disorders all cause growth failure and are far more common than GH deficiency. Only after these are ruled out does evaluation proceed to IGF-1 measurement and bone age, with provocative testing and imaging reserved for later steps.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Treatment is started only after a diagnosis is established, and GH for short children with normal GH is controversial.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IGFBP-3 supplements IGF-1 in uncertain cases and does not replace excluding commoner causes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MRI is obtained once GH deficiency has been confirmed, to look for a sellar mass.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Provocative GH testing is the gold standard but is reserved for uncertain cases after commoner causes are excluded and IGF-1 is checked.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man who underwent resection of a craniopharyngioma and pituitary irradiation reports fatigue, reduced muscle mass, and increased abdominal fat. His serum IGF-1 concentration is at the low end of the age- and sex-specific reference range. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to establish the diagnosis of growth hormone deficiency?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Administer an oral glucose load and measure growth hormone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Measure a random serum growth hormone concentration

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain a dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry scan of the hip

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perform provocative growth hormone stimulation testing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat the IGF-1 level in 12 months to track the trend

explanation.summary: In hypothalamic-pituitary disease with a low-normal IGF-1, provocative GH testing is required to diagnose GH deficiency.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adult GH deficiency can be confirmed on IGF-1 alone only when the level falls below the age- and sex-specific lower limit of normal. When IGF-1 is low to normal, as here, provocative testing with agents that should trigger GH release is required; a failure of GH to rise indicates deficiency. Testing is appropriate in this patient because known hypothalamic-pituitary disease makes deficiency likely.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glucose suppression tests for GH excess, which is the opposite of the problem suspected here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A single random GH level is uninterpretable because secretion is pulsatile.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bone densitometry characterizes a consequence of the deficiency and cannot establish it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Deferring diagnosis for a year does not resolve an indeterminate IGF-1 in a patient with known pituitary disease.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man is evaluated for coarsening facial features, an enlarging jaw with newly spaced teeth, and hoarseness. His serum IGF-1 concentration is elevated. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Measure growth hormone after a dose of oral clonidine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Measure growth hormone after an arginine infusion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Measure growth hormone after an oral glucose load

choices.label: D
choices.text: Measure growth hormone after an overnight fast

choices.label: E
choices.text: Measure growth hormone after insulin-induced hypoglycemia

explanation.summary: Elevated IGF-1 is confirmed as GH excess by failure of GH to suppress after a glucose load.
explanation.whyCorrect: IGF-1 is the best initial test but produces false positives, so a GH suppression test follows. Glucose normally suppresses GH secretion; if GH levels remain high after the glucose load, autonomous GH production is confirmed and pituitary MRI is then obtained to find the adenoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clonidine is another provocative stimulus used in GH stimulation testing for deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Arginine is a provocative agent used to stimulate GH release when deficiency is suspected.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fasting and hypoglycemia raise GH physiologically and would not demonstrate autonomous secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Insulin-induced hypoglycemia provokes GH secretion and is used in the workup of deficiency.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy has short stature, marked obesity from constant food seeking, and a history of severe hypotonia in infancy. He has cognitive and behavioral difficulties, and testing shows growth hormone deficiency and hypogonadism. Which of the following is the most likely underlying abnormality?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoimmune destruction of anterior pituitary tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autosomal recessive mutation of the growth hormone receptor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deletion involving chromosome 15

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of one X chromosome with gonadal dysgenesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Somatotroph adenoma of the anterior pituitary

explanation.summary: Prader-Willi syndrome, from a chromosome 15 deletion, causes hyperphagic obesity with short stature, hypotonia, and GH deficiency.
explanation.whyCorrect: Prader-Willi syndrome is a genetic cause of obesity linked to deletions on chromosome 15. Affected children have hyperphagia, obesity, short stature, hypotonia, and cognitive and behavioral difficulties, along with hormone abnormalities that frequently include GH deficiency and hypogonadism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoimmune pituitary damage is an acquired cause of GH deficiency and does not produce this syndromic picture.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A GH receptor mutation causes Laron syndrome, marked by severe growth failure with high GH and low IGF-1, not hyperphagic obesity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Turner syndrome causes short stature but not the hyperphagia, hypotonia, and behavioral phenotype described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A somatotroph adenoma causes GH excess with excessive linear growth in a child.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman with acromegaly has persistently elevated IGF-1 after incomplete resection of a pituitary macroadenoma. Pegvisomant is started, and her physician schedules serial pituitary imaging. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activates inhibitory somatostatin receptors on pituitary somatotrophs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blocks growth hormone receptors in peripheral target tissues

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blocks hepatic uptake of IGF-1 by target tissue receptors

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibits release of growth hormone-releasing hormone from the hypothalamus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stimulates dopamine receptors on somatotroph adenoma cells

explanation.summary: Pegvisomant is a peripheral GH receptor blocker, so it lowers IGF-1 without acting on the adenoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: By blocking GH receptors in peripheral tissues, pegvisomant prevents GH signaling and reduces IGF-1 production. Because it works downstream and does not suppress GH secretion or target the pituitary tumor itself, tumor size must be monitored separately with imaging, which is why serial scans were scheduled.

whyWrongByChoice.A: That is the mechanism of octreotide, a somatostatin analog acting at the pituitary.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The drug blocks GH receptors and reduces IGF-1 production rather than blocking IGF-1 uptake.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pegvisomant acts on peripheral GH receptors, not on hypothalamic releasing hormone secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dopamine receptor agonism describes cabergoline, which suppresses GH secretion from some adenomas.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man with a GH-secreting pituitary adenoma is found to have a fasting plasma glucose of 168 mg/dL and elevated serum free fatty acids. Which of the following best explains these metabolic findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells by circulating GH

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess cortisol secretion from the same pituitary adenoma cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Impaired intestinal absorption of glucose from soft tissue overgrowth

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased hepatic gluconeogenesis and lipolysis with antagonism of insulin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced hepatic IGF-1 output leading to impaired glucose uptake

explanation.summary: GH excess causes secondary diabetes mellitus by raising glucose and driving lipolysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: GH normally raises serum glucose by increasing hepatic gluconeogenesis, increasing lipolysis and lipid oxidation, and antagonizing insulin. When GH is chronically elevated, blood glucose stays high and free fatty acids rise, producing secondary diabetes mellitus and contributing to accelerated atherosclerosis and heart disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hyperglycemia here results from GH's counter-regulatory actions, not autoimmune beta-cell destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Some adenomas cosecrete prolactin or ACTH, but the described glucose and fatty acid pattern is explained by GH itself.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Malabsorption of glucose would lower rather than raise fasting plasma glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IGF-1 is elevated in GH excess, not reduced, and the hyperglycemia comes from GH's metabolic effects.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy is brought in because he is far taller than his classmates and has continued to grow rapidly over the past 2 years. He has headaches. His serum IGF-1 is elevated, and MRI shows a sellar mass. Which of the following best explains his excessive linear growth?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A connective tissue disorder producing disproportionate long bones

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess growth hormone secreted after the epiphyseal plates fuse

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excess growth hormone secreted before the epiphyseal plates fuse

choices.label: D
choices.text: Familial tall stature with an accelerated pubertal growth spurt

choices.label: E
choices.text: Precocious puberty with early sex steroid exposure

explanation.summary: Gigantism is GH excess occurring while the epiphyseal growth plates are still open.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gigantism refers to excess GH secretion from the anterior pituitary before the epiphyseal growth plates fuse, producing excessive linear growth and taller-than-expected stature. It is usually caused by a pituitary adenoma and is typically diagnosed around puberty, when the abnormal growth becomes obvious. Untreated, these patients go on to develop acromegalic features as adults.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Marfan syndrome causes tall stature through connective tissue abnormality, with a normal IGF-1.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GH excess after plate fusion causes acromegaly without further gain in height, which does not fit a still-growing adolescent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Familial tall stature does not raise IGF-1 or produce a sellar mass with headaches.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Precocious puberty is a commoner cause of overgrowth but does not explain the elevated IGF-1 and pituitary mass.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman has biochemically confirmed growth hormone excess, and MRI demonstrates a discrete pituitary adenoma. She has no contraindication to anesthesia and is willing to pursue any recommended therapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cabergoline therapy with periodic IGF-1 monitoring

choices.label: B
choices.text: Octreotide therapy with periodic IGF-1 monitoring

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pegvisomant therapy with periodic tumor imaging

choices.label: D
choices.text: Radiation therapy directed at the pituitary adenoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surgical resection of the pituitary adenoma

explanation.summary: Surgical resection is first-line therapy for a GH-secreting pituitary adenoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Removing the adenoma addresses the source of hormone directly, and as GH and IGF-1 fall to normal after surgery the soft tissue changes gradually revert. Medical therapy is reserved for patients whose levels do not normalize with surgery, whose tumor cannot be completely resected, or who cannot or will not undergo an operation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cabergoline is a secondary option, most useful when residual IGF-1 elevation is mild.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Octreotide is used when surgery fails to normalize GH and IGF-1 or is not an option.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pegvisomant treats persistent hormonal excess downstream and leaves the tumor itself untreated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiation is considered when disease persists despite surgery and medication.
